finding: First independent multi-subject empirical validation of SUBJECT-01 macroscopic aerobic bioenergetic coupling on PhysioNet ACTES cycloergometer dataset (SRC-0073, DOI 10.13026/2qs3-kh43, 52,062 synchronized beat-to-beat records across N=18 adolescent athletes): (1) Under strict Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation with frozen parameters (eta_gross in [0.18, 0.28], c_ox = 20,900 J/L, tau = 35.0 s), the dynamic bioenergetic ODE with body-mass allometric scaling achieves cross-subject out-of-sample R2 = 0.7371 +/- 0.1770 (RMSE = 0.290 +/- 0.059 L/min), vastly outperforming empirical static linear M1 (R2 = 0.4045, RMSE = 0.416 L/min) and null static M0 (R2 = -0.8343, RMSE = 0.773 L/min). (2) Allometric mass normalization improves out-of-sample generalizability by +0.131 R2 relative to unscaled population parameters across a 39.7 to 89.9 kg cohort. (3) Macro-metabolic coupling is validated across independent human subjects, resolving the single-subject limitation of Rehman 2024. (4) Crucially, whole-body pulmonary VO2 does NOT observe or validate intramuscular high-energy phosphates ([PCr], [Pi], [ATP]), cytosolic pH, motor unit recruitment rates, or quadriceps PCSA; TARGET-CPE45 remains NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED and biological interventions NO_GO.
notes: Overcomes the N=1 bottleneck of Rehman 2024. Confirms macroscopic generalizability of aerobic energy coupling while rigorously enforcing the unobservability of compartmental intracellular states.
